prompt: An angle of $-50^\circ$ is drawn in standard position (a $50^\circ$ turn clockwise). What is the smallest positive angle coterminal with it? Give just the number of degrees.
hint: A negative angle turns clockwise, but it still stops somewhere a counterclockwise angle could reach.

hints.text: A negative angle turns clockwise, but it still stops somewhere a counterclockwise angle could reach.

explanation: Turning $50^\circ$ clockwise lands just below the positive $x$-axis, in Quadrant IV.
To name that same spot with a positive angle, add a full turn: $-50^\circ + 360^\circ = 310^\circ$.
Both angles finish on the same ray, so they are coterminal.

alternativeExplanations.title: Going the long way around
steps: Backing up $50^\circ$ from the start gets you to the same ray as going forward all the way around minus that $50^\circ$.
Forward all the way around is $360^\circ$, so the long way is $360^\circ - 50^\circ = 310^\circ$.
